A confidence interval is a statistical tool that provides a range of values within which a parameter of interest is expected to lie, with a certain level of confidence. Confidence intervals are calculated based on sample data and can be used to estimate the characteristics of a population, such as the average height of a population or the average age of a population. Confidence intervals are important because they give a range of values that are likely to contain the true population parameter with a specified level of confidence, rather than just a single value. The level of confidence is usually expressed as a percentage, and is usually between 0% and 100%.[1] "A confidence interval is a statistical tool that provides a range of values within which a parameter of interest is expected to lie, with a certain level of confidence.
